First, researchers use a process called standardization. They administer the rest to a representative sample of the population to be tested.

Each individual who takes the test must take it under the same conditions as the sample group. This establishes the standards to which individual scores are compared.

68 percent of IQ scores from the WAIS III range between 1 SD above or below 100 (1 SD is 15 points). So approximately 68 percent of those in the sample have IQs between 85 and 115. 2 percent score over 140, .2 percent over 145. 9 percent over 120. 100 is the average, below 70 is mental retardation.

To compute the IQ score, you take the ratio of the mental age to the chronological age and multiply by 100. If a 10 year old child has a mental age of 12, he has a 120 IQ. If a 10 year old had a mental age of 8, he has an 80 IQ. Scores where the mental age and chronological age match, that is average.
